questions.def: Use quotation marks to show someone is speaking.
questions.question: She said, ___ I am happy to be here.

questions.def: Use a comma before 'and' to separate items in a list.
questions.question: I like apples___ bananas.

questions.def: The sentence needs the base form of the verb 'want'.
questions.question: I ___ (want) to go home early today.

questions.def: An ellipsis shows words are missing or not finished.
questions.question: Do you like to ___ go swimming?

questions.def: 'Because' explains the reason she works at a school.
questions.question: She works at a school___ she likes kids.

questions.def: The sentence needs the past tense form of the verb 'say'.
questions.question: She ___ (say), "Hello!"

questions.def: Use a comma to separate items in a list.
questions.question: I need to buy milk___ eggs, and bread.

questions.def: Use a colon to introduce a direct quote.
questions.question: He asked___ "Are you coming?"

questions.def: The sentence needs the present continuous form 'is working'.
questions.question: She is ___ (work) hard today.

questions.def: Use a question mark at the end of a question.
questions.question: What time is it___

questions.def: 'Because' gives the reason why he can't go.
questions.question: I can't go___ I am busy.

questions.def: The sentence needs the present perfect form 'has eaten'.
questions.question: He ___ (eat) dinner already.

questions.def: 's' shows possession.
questions.question: That is my sister___ car.

questions.def: 'And' connects two similar ideas.
questions.question: I want to go to Italy___ France.

questions.def: The sentence needs the past simple form 'made'.
questions.question: They ___ (make) a cake yesterday.

questions.def: A semicolon connects related independent clauses.
questions.question: She likes to read books___ she learns a lot.

questions.def: 'Because' explains the reason he is happy.
questions.question: He is happy___ he got a good grade.

questions.def: 'Its' should be 'It's' (It is) or 'Its' (possessive).
questions.question: Its a beautiful day to go outside and play.

questions.def: The sentence needs the future form 'am going'.
questions.question: I ___ (go) to the store tomorrow.

questions.def: Use an exclamation mark for strong emotion.
questions.question: Help___ I'm falling!

questions.def: 'But' shows a contrast between the two preferences.
questions.question: He likes tea___ I prefer coffee.

questions.def: The sentence needs the present perfect form 'has lived'.
questions.question: She ___ (live) here for five years.

questions.def: Use a comma to introduce a question in indirect speech.
questions.question: She asked___ Are you ready?

questions.def: 'Because' explains the reason why he is tired.
questions.question: He is tired___ he worked all day.

questions.def: A comma separates independent clauses joined by 'but'. 'Bananas' is plural.
questions.question: I like apples, but I don't like ___.

questions.def: Use quotation marks to show the exact words someone said.
questions.question: He said, ___ 'I am going home'.

questions.def: 'Think' is a stative verb and simple present is appropriate here.
questions.question: I ___ it's a good idea.

questions.def: A question mark goes at the end of a question.
questions.question: Are you going to the park___

questions.def: Commas separate items in a list.
questions.question: I like dogs___ cats, and birds.

questions.def: Use 'said' (past tense) to introduce quoted speech.
questions.question: He ___, 'I want to go home'.
